ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.89 to the rider's original payment method; send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route compliance record (no formal warning, first such incident); record a driver violation under RD-2 (no traffic reason) — no repeat breach, so no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was billed on 14.9 km against an optimal 10.7 km, a +4.2 km deviation, and the single off-route segment is F3 (21:43–21:50, 5.14 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.44 km, adding 3.70 km over Jalan Bukit Merah → Kampong Bahru Road → Telok Blangah Road → Henderson Road) [F1][F3][RD-1]. The deviation is over the 1 km tolerance, so the RD-2 matrix applies [F4][RD-2].

The traffic screen is settled against the driver: the replaced stretch, Ayer Rajah Expressway, was in speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) throughout the trip window, Central Expressway in band 8, and no incident, closure or heavy congestion is recorded [F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. The trace marks RD-4 ✗, so this is a no-traffic-reason case: excess distance fare refundable and a driver violation recorded [RD-2].

Consent is the decisive element and the record settles it. At 21:40 the driver asked, "mind if I go round via Telok Blangah Road?" [F7]; at 21:40 the rider answered "No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway" [F8]. Before the segment began at 21:43 the rider had refused the alternative; the chat is complete and every message timestamped [F10]; and no rider message agrees. RD-5 requires the rider's own message sent before or at the start of the segment — a driver's account written after the trip is not consent, and here the driver's own words admit he took the route anyway [F11][RD-5]. The rider's 21:44 message, "Why you go this way?? I said stay," confirms there was no agreement [F9][RD-5]. The rider named no road he was agreeing to (he named one he ruled out), so nothing is tied to the segment; RD-3 gives no exemption because no rider message named a place the car went to and no stop was measured [F3][F7][F8][RD-3].

Amount: 4.18 km deviation (billed distance − optimal route) less 0 km exempt = 4.18 km × $1.4098/km = $5.893... ≈ $5.89, exactly the trace formula [F4][RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; surge was 1.0× in any event [F5][F6][RD-2].

Driver profile: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6 flag_account is not triggered, and profile facts never decide the case [F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read all three chat messages, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint. They contain a route argument and mild frustration ("Why you go this way?? I said stay. I'm late already.") [F9], but no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and no accident or injury is described [F7][F8][F9][F11][F12][F14]. safety_concern = none.

Evidence: the GPS track, fare breakdown, complete timestamped chat and traffic record settle every element this ruling needs (deviation, consent, traffic reason), so evidence_status = sufficient.
